title: One repository behind the whole CV site

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's a site that holds a CV in two languages, a PDF version, a machine-readable resume and a blog. And it all comes out of one repository.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a lot to keep in sync.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the point of the project. The bilingual CV pages are static HTML. The PDFs are written in LaTeX. The resume also exists as structured data, and there's a Hugo blog on top.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So how does it all get published?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A local script builds and validates both the CV and the blog, then publishes them together from the docs folder on the main branch. One command, one result.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The project describes itself as a high-performance, accessible, bilingual portfolio with zero runtime overhead. Nothing runs on a server when you open it, so it loads fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, and that's fun. JavaScript, HTML, Python and TeX each make up a real share of the code. It's mostly the build tooling and the pages themselves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's automated checking in the pipeline, with Python's unittest among the tools. The full write-up on the page explains the publishing paths.
